target.title: fix(onboard): skip unavailable skill installers via lifecycle readiness preflight
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Takeover of #99652 (credit to @Sedrak-Hovhannisyan for the report, the grouped-note UX, and the base implementation — the original commit is preserved with authorship in this branch).

Fresh Linux/VPS onboarding can end in a wall of optional skill dependency failures: the trusted bundled skill step attempts brew-, Go-, and uv-backed recipes even when Homebrew is missing, Go is older than 1.21 (newer `go` module directives fail), or uv is absent. #99652 fixed the noise by gating readiness inside onboarding, but its onboarding-local gate disabled the shared installer's existing apt-get Go bootstrap (`installGoViaApt` handles root and passwordless sudo on Debian/Ubuntu), turning a supported automatic path into manual work on the exact fresh-VPS scenario it targets.

AI-assisted: yes (Claude Code takeover rework; original PR authored with Codex).

## Why This Change Was Made

Installer capability knowledge now has a single owner. `src/skills/lifecycle/install.ts` exports `resolveInstallerKindReadiness`, a preflight twin of `installSkill`'s real fallbacks:

- **brew**: ready when any brew executable resolves (installSkill swaps `argv[0]` to the resolved path, so off-PATH Linuxbrew works for brew recipes).
- **uv**: ready when `uv` is on PATH or brew is on PATH (mirrors `ensureUvInstalled`; off-PATH brew is not enough because the recipe still spawns bare `uv`).
- **go**: existing Go must be 1.21+ (installSkill never re-bootstraps over an existing toolchain); missing Go is ready via on-PATH brew, or via apt-get when root/passwordless sudo is available — preserving the `installGoViaApt` path #99652 dropped. A visible apt candidate older than 1.21 (Ubuntu 22.04 ships 1.18, Debian 12 ships 1.19) is vetoed; an absent candidate defers to the installer, which refreshes indexes first (fresh containers with cleared apt lists).

Onboarding (`src/commands/onboard-skills.ts`) consumes the preflight, keeps #99652's grouped "Manual skill prerequisites" note and localized strings, and drops its duplicated brew/Go/uv detection.

## User Impact

Fresh onboarding stays calm: recipes that cannot succeed are skipped into one actionable note instead of failing one-by-one, while everything the shared installer can genuinely bootstrap (brew-based uv/Go installs, apt-get Go on Debian/Ubuntu as root or with passwordless sudo) still installs automatically. Non-onboarding install paths (`openclaw skills install`, doctor) are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/onboard-skills.test.ts src/skills/lifecycle/install-fallback.test.ts` — 24 tests pass, including new preflight coverage: apt bootstrap as root, passwordless sudo, too-old apt candidate vetoed, absent candidate deferred, off-PATH Linuxbrew rejected for uv/go but kept for brew recipes, too-old local Go skipped.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check` on touched files; `git diff --check` clean.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json` on touched files — clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` — clean.
- Structured Codex review (gpt-5.5, branch vs upstream/main) ran three cycles; both P2 findings (off-PATH brew false positive, unversioned apt candidate) and the P1 follow-up (unrefreshed apt cache false negative) were fixed with regression tests; final run: "patch is correct (0.91), no actionable findings".
- Known gap: no recorded fresh Linux/VPS end-to-end onboarding transcript yet (same ask ClawSweeper posted on #99652). The unit layer covers the readiness matrix; happy to run a Crabbox/Testbox fresh-container onboarding lane as follow-up proof before merge.

Supersedes #99652.
